headline_cluster.headline: הרבה יותר ישראלים מוכרים בהפסד את הדירה שקנו: המספרים ב–24 ערים נחשפים
המספרים מוכיחים: הרבה יותר ישראלים מוכרים בהפסד את הדירה שלהם

primary_source.description: TheMarker's own analysis of the Israel Tax Authority real-estate transaction database (nadlan.gov.il): second-hand sales in 24 cities, Jan 2022 - 17 Sep 2026, outlier transactions filtered, sale price compared to the seller's purchase price after inflation (CPI) adjustment. No standalone published dataset/methodology note found; nadlan.gov.il blocked by audit egress proxy and the purchase-sale pairing is not reproducible from here.

context_sources.name: Finance Ministry Chief Economist - quarterly housing-market reviews (investor sales at real capital loss)
context_sources.relevance: Independent official series on a different population (investor sales only). Reported ~14% record around 2020 (Beer Sheva area 24.3% of investor sales in Q4 2020 per BizPortal), 10.6% in Q2 2024 (highest since 2020, +~4pp y/y), 10.5% in Q1 2025; Beer Sheva consistently the top city, followed by southern cities (Eilat, Kiryat Gat). Read via search-engine summaries only (gov.il, globes, ynet, bizportal blocked).

clustering_note: Same article ID (000001a0-f7af-de31-a7f0-ffbf67b50000) syndicated on themarker.com and haaretz.co.il/tmr (sister outlets) - one piece, not independent corroboration. TheMarker's own real-estate data-journalism analysis, breaking down loss-sales by city (24 cities); likely sourced from Israel Tax Authority / CBS real-estate transaction data or a real-estate data provider (Madlan/Nadlan).

claims.claim: הרבה יותר ישראלים מוכרים בהפסד את הדירה שקנו
claims.evidence: Per search-indexed body text, the 'loss' is a REAL (inflation-adjusted) loss: sale price below purchase price after CPI adjustment. With cumulative Israeli CPI inflation of roughly 15%+ since 2022, a large share of these 'loss' sales can be nominal gains. The headline drops the 'real' qualifier, so a reader would take it as selling for less shekels than paid. The direction ('many more') is consistent with the article's own series (2.8% in 2022 -> 4.7% 2024 -> 8.7% 2025 -> 11.1% in 2026 YTD) and with the Chief Economist's investor series rising to ~10.5% in 2024-25.

claims.claim: Across the 24 cities the real-loss sale rate rose from 2.8% (2022) to 4.7% (2024), 8.7% (2025) and 11.1% (2026 to 17 Sep) - roughly a fourfold increase
claims.evidence: Figures are TheMarker's own computation from the Tax Authority database; underlying data not reachable/reproducible from the audit environment. Directionally consistent with the Finance Ministry Chief Economist investor series. Context: the 2022 baseline is the peak-boom year (a trough for loss-sales); the Chief Economist reported ~14% real-loss investor sales around 2020, so 'many more vs 2022' holds but levels are not unprecedented. No evidence the article claims a historic record.

claims.claim: City ranking 2026: Beer Sheva 24.3%, Ashdod 19.1%, Tel Aviv 15.8% (above the 11.1% average, third)
claims.evidence: Not verifiable without the underlying data. Beer Sheva leading is consistent with every Chief Economist review found. Flag: 24.3% for Beer Sheva also appears in BizPortal's summary of the Chief Economist's Q4 2020 investor data - likely coincidence, but these numbers reached the audit only via search-engine snippets of the paywalled article, so a snippet/summarizer conflation cannot be ruled out.

claims.claim: המספרים מוכיחים: הרבה יותר ישראלים מוכרים בהפסד את הדירה שלהם
claims.evidence: Same syndicated article as TheMarker (not independent). Same issue: 'loss' is an inflation-adjusted real loss; headline omits this. The 'numbers prove' wording is framing and not judged; the claim is also a 24-city sample of second-hand deals with prior-purchase data, not all Israelis' sales.

claims.claim: Same body figures as TheMarker (2.8% -> 11.1%; Beer Sheva 24.3%, Ashdod 19.1%, Tel Aviv 15.8%)
claims.evidence: Identical syndicated body (same CMS ID); see TheMarker body claims. Recorded once per outlet, not independent corroboration.

audit_note: Both article URLs (themarker.com, haaretz.co.il) blocked by the audit environment's egress proxy (CONNECT 403), so body_ok=0 for both; body figures come only from search-engine snippets of the TheMarker page (own analysis of Tax Authority transaction DB, 24 cities, Jan 2022 - 17 Sep 2026, outliers filtered, inflation-adjusted). The primary data (nadlan.gov.il) and the Chief Economist's gov.il reports were also unreachable; context figures came via search summaries of Globes/BizPortal/Mako/ynet. Main finding: headlines in both outlets say 'selling at a loss' while the analysis measures REAL (CPI-adjusted) loss - imprecise, since many such sales are nominal gains. Trend direction is plausible and corroborated by an independent official series; exact numbers and city ranking unverifiable. One syndicated piece, not two independent reports. Re-run with outlet/gov.il access to upgrade to complete.
